_help: Policy for the customer support persona (Lumen Cloud, gated action: send_email to a customer). Every threshold carries a one-sentence 'why' citing business_rules.md.
on_ezio_failure_why: If Ezio is down, slow past our retries, or malformed we fail closed to HOLD because rule 6 makes Ezio the only fact-checker for public claims (laws, regulations) and tone, so the email can't go out unreviewed; but a price or policy our own data proves wrong is still BLOCKED, since that evidence doesn't depend on Ezio.
tier_decisions_why: GREEN approves only after our price-sheet/policy check and the per-dimension minimums also pass (GREEN with accuracy not_scored proves nothing on its own); YELLOW and RED without a specific contradiction signal a tone/flattery problem, which rule 4 says is a HOLD, while any contradicted claim (Ezio's per rule 6, or our data's per rule 1) is a BLOCK regardless of tier.

tone.why: The mock takes 10 points per '!' and 6 per hype word or all-caps word, so 70 lets a friendly 'Thanks for reaching out!' through but holds over-the-top hype (the practice hype email scores 26), per rule 4; our own hype-word check backs this up.

bias.why: One one-sided phrase ('obviously', 'everyone knows') drops bias to 85, and an email to a customer shouldn't argue one side, so a single instance gets a manager's look per rule 4.

agreement.why: One flattering phrase ('you're absolutely right', 'great question') drops agreement to 75; rule 4 says flattery or agreeing with a customer's claim is a HOLD even when every number is right.

when_accuracy_not_scored_why: Ezio can't see Lumen Cloud's prices or policies, so not_scored is normal for our claims and our own check is the accuracy signal; rule 5 says an email with no checkable claims is fine to send and a missing accuracy score is not a reason to block.
when_accuracy_unavailable_why: When Ezio's fact-check is down we approve only if every sentence contains a price, discount, refund, trial, or response-time figure our data verified (nothing left for Ezio to check); otherwise we HOLD per rule 6, because an unchecked public claim (e.g. about GDPR) could be wrong.
source_of_truth_why: Our checker (support_check.py) BLOCKS any price, discount, refund window, trial, or first-response time that contradicts price_sheet.csv or policies.json (rule 1); BLOCKS a loyalty discount the customer's plan or tenure in context doesn't qualify for, any stacked discount, and any price quoted for custom-priced Enterprise (rule 2); and HOLDS promises of product features, delivery dates, or exceptions for a manager (rule 3).

fact_sheet_tolerances.why: Used only by the financial_analyst checker (fact_check.py); customer-support prices, percentages, and day/hour counts must match the price sheet and policies exactly (to the cent).
